requirement: Short links expire after a week. Redirect analytics are retained indefinitely. Expired links should still redirect for trusted partners.

stateTransitions.reason: material ambiguity detected; awaiting human clarification

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: The clause allowing 'requests identified as originating from a trusted partner' to bypass the 7-day expiration rule never states how a request is identified as a trusted partner, nor which system or actor maintains that determination (IP allowlist, API key, mutual TLS certificate, signed header, or a partner-account flag on the short link itself).
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Checked both requirement statements and the analytics requirement for any schema, contract, or referenced policy that defines 'trusted partner'; none exists in the normalized set. Checked for a companion actor/role definition (e.g., an auth service or partner registry) and found none.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: The requirement that a short link 'SHALL expire exactly 7 days (168 hours) after its creation timestamp' does not state whether a standard request arriving at exactly the 168-hour boundary instant is treated as still-valid (inclusive) or already-expired (exclusive).
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Looked for a stated comparison operator (e.g. 'at or after', 'strictly after') or a validation/test target that pins the boundary; the statement only gives a duration, not an inclusive/exclusive rule, and no other artifact in the set addresses it.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: Requirement 1's standard-path clause says an expired link 'SHALL no longer resolve/redirect to its target URL', while the trusted-partner clause requires the system to 'continue to redirect an expired short link to its original target URL' for trusted partners — meaning the target-URL mapping must still exist and be readable after the 7-day mark. Read in isolation, the standard-path wording is compatible with hard-deleting the link record at expiration, which would make the trusted-partner bypass impossible to implement.
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Cross-read both FUNCTIONAL requirements together (both share externalId '1') to see whether the data-lifecycle question — soft-expire flag with retained mapping vs. hard deletion of the underlying record — is settled anywhere; it is not, and no schema or domain invariant in the provided set fixes short-link storage lifecycle.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: The non-functional requirement that 'redirect analytics records (e.g., click/redirect events...)' be retained indefinitely does not state whether a blocked/denied access attempt made by a standard requester against an already-expired link itself generates an analytics record, or whether analytics capture stops once a link is expired for that requester class.
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Checked whether 'click/redirect events' is defined to include failed/denied attempts as well as successful redirects; the requirement only discusses retention of records already created, not which events qualify for creation post-expiration, and no other requirement addresses it.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: The phrase 'associated metadata' in the analytics retention requirement is given only via a non-exhaustive example ('e.g., click/redirect events and associated metadata') and never enumerates which fields (requester IP, user agent, geolocation, partner identity, etc.) are in scope for indefinite, undeletable retention.
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Searched the normalized set for an analytics schema or data-classification artifact that would fix the metadata field list; none is present, and 'e.g.' explicitly signals the list is illustrative rather than closed, so the retained field set is a genuine open fork with data-retention/compliance consequences.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: Requirement 1's reference to a short link's 'creation timestamp' does not state clock source, timezone, or precision (e.g., server UTC time in milliseconds vs. seconds).
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Checked whether any stated obligation (the 168-hour expiry check, the analytics retention rule, or any validation target) depends on the specific timezone or precision chosen, rather than merely on elapsed duration from a single consistently-used timestamp.
s3RealResponse.noClarificationReason: The expiry rule is purely relative (168 hours elapsed since that same stored timestamp), so any conformant choice of clock representation (UTC vs. local, second vs. millisecond precision) produces identical elapsed-time behavior; this is the ordinary, uncontested default for a server-generated creation timestamp and no approved obligation distinguishes between the choices.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: The term 'short link' itself is used throughout both functional requirements without a formal definition of its structure (e.g., encoding, length, character set).
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Checked whether the expiration behavior, trusted-partner bypass, or analytics retention rules depend on any specific short-link format or encoding; none of the three requirements reference the link's internal structure, only its resolve/redirect behavior and lifecycle.
s3RealResponse.noClarificationReason: The ordinary, plain-language meaning of 'short link' (an alias that redirects to a longer target URL) fully suffices to implement all three stated requirements; no obligation in the set constrains link format, so every conformant encoding choice behaves identically with respect to expiration, bypass, and analytics.

s2RealResponse.statement: A short link SHALL expire exactly 7 days (168 hours) after its creation timestamp, after which point it SHALL no longer resolve/redirect to its target URL for standard (non-trusted-partner) requesters.
For requests identified as originating from a trusted partner, the system SHALL continue to redirect an expired short link to its original target URL, bypassing the standard 7-day expiration rule.

Redirect analytics records (e.g., click/redirect events and associated metadata) SHALL be retained indefinitely and SHALL NOT be deleted or purged as a consequence of the associated short link's expiration.
